author: Dale Yurong
title: Dine and Dish: Bulle in Northwest Fresno - NewsBreak
text:
By Dale Yurong ,
2 hours ago
The open kitchen at Bulle at Herndon and Marks in northwest Fresno is fire!
"Taking California cuisine and trying to improve it," says co-owner Tom Miller. "Level up."
Tom gave us a look at their prime filet, which they source from the Midwest.
"And then we have what we call a Robuchon potato, which is a very creamy potato and asparagus," he said.
Steaks feature a Japanese seasoning.
"Shio kombu is basically dried seaweed and kelp," Miller said.
They also showed a twist on their mac-and-cheese, which is used with gruyere cheese.
"A lot of our philosophy going forward is trying to keep things simple," says Beverage Director Shane Tolmasoff. "Go back to the roots of cocktails."
Tolmasoff made a "Golden Hour," using a shrub of champagne, vinegar and honey.
"We actually get bubbles made out of a bunch of different sugars," he said.
Bulle is French for "bubble."
Co-owner Davita Miller said her the Waygu burger has been one of her favorites, with parmesan fries.
The Wagyu burger is thick, juicy and messy.
"We think we've struck paydirt with this one," Tom said. "We want to be approachable to everybody."
The wedge salad is popular, and the Japanese milk bread can't be missed.
"One of the most popular dishes is our Iberico ham toast," Tom said.
The Prime New York striploin is crusted.
"Just like any restaurant in town, you evolve," Tom said.
